recent_posts.title: AI website builder for static site generators?
recent_posts.summary: Themefisher is developing an AI-powered website builder that generates static sites using frameworks like Hugo, Astro, and Next.js. The tool aims to bridge the gap between AI website builders and traditional static site generators by automating the entire workflow: generating sites from prompts using pre-built components, creating GitHub repositories, and configuring deployment to platforms like Vercel or Netlify. The product includes a built-in CMS for content management and allows code export, targeting both non-technical users and developers who want to skip initial setup.

recent_posts.title: Anyone else struggling to let non-technical clients edit SSG sites easily?
recent_posts.summary: A development team shares their experience building websites with static site generators like Hugo, Astro, and Next.js, highlighting the challenge of enabling non-technical clients and content writers to edit content. Traditional workflows involving markdown files, Git, and code editors proved too complex for users accustomed to tools like Google Docs. After trying various solutions including documentation and existing CMS options, they built Sitepins, a Git-based CMS tool that simplifies content editing for non-technical users while maintaining the benefits of static site generators.

recent_posts.title: Webflow App Gen is live. It is powered by Astro
recent_posts.summary: Webflow launched App Gen, a new tool powered by Astro framework. Early testing reveals the product handles core functionality but has significant bugs including a problematic code editor, disappearing changes after saves, unexpected page resets, limited search capabilities, and missing image attachment features. Despite these issues, the choice of Astro as the underlying technology is promising.

recent_posts.title: Astro Starllight is officially the best in class, backed by real-world user data.
recent_posts.summary: Starlight, Astro's documentation framework, ranks first among major documentation tools in HTTP Archive's Tech Report. The framework achieved near-perfect scores across Core Web Vitals, accessibility, and SEO metrics, outperforming competitors like Docusaurus and VitePress in real-world performance measurements.

recent_posts.title: Turn your static site visually editable for non-technical clients & teammates
recent_posts.summary: Sitepins is a visual CMS that connects to Git repositories, enabling non-technical users to edit static site content without code. It supports popular static site generators like Astro, Next.js, and Hugo, offers a WYSIWYG editor with Markdown support, maintains Git version control, includes media management, and features AI-powered content generation. The tool allows developers to maintain their workflow while giving clients and teammates direct content editing capabilities.

recent_posts.title: AstroJS Course (Beginner → Intermediate) by Lukasz Adam—$19.
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive beginner-to-intermediate course covering AstroJS fundamentals including setup, routing, components, CSS styling, React integration, SEO optimization, deployment strategies, and headless CMS integration. The course includes practical projects and covers modern web development practices with Astro framework.

recent_posts.title: Webflow donates $150K to Astro + picks Astro to power its upcoming AI app code gen
recent_posts.summary: Webflow has donated $150,000 to become an official sponsor of Astro and will use the framework as the default for its upcoming AI code generation feature. The partnership enables building production-ready web apps and reusable components, with full-stack applications visually designed in Webflow and coded with Astro for deployment on Cloudflare's edge network.

recent_posts.title: 36+ Astro Themes only for $137 (One-time Payment)
recent_posts.summary: Themefisher offers a bundle of 33+ premium Astro themes for $137 as a one-time purchase, including all future themes. The collection covers various use cases like SaaS landing pages, documentation sites, blogs, and business websites, all built with Astro and Tailwind CSS. The bundle includes commercial licensing, free updates, priority support, and detailed documentation for each theme.

recent_posts.title: Astro will be at ViteConf 2025
recent_posts.summary: Astro will participate in ViteConf 2025, the official in-person conference for Vite organized in collaboration with Evan You and the Vite core team. The conference will take place in Amsterdam.

recent_posts.title: Sitepins - Git-based CMS for Sites Built with Astro, Next.js, Hugo & more.
recent_posts.summary: Sitepins is a free Git-based headless CMS designed for static site generators like Astro, Next.js, and Hugo. It allows developers to maintain their Git workflow while providing non-technical users with a visual web interface for content editing. All changes are committed through Git, preserving version control and developer oversight.
